I also grepped all OAI uses of the four declarations in the target: only directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule has downstream uses, all inside this file, while the related jet/dualEvalLie interface is used in GradedNormalizedRelativeLog.lean. The target contains no `@[simp]` attributes and no sanity-problematic general `simp` calls; its only `simp` uses are `simpa only` with explicit lists, so the main simp-interface issue is the missing canonical projection/normal-form lemmas for first jets, evidenced by four hand-written `change`+`rw` blocks. Because I cannot run Lean, the exact simp-normal forms of the proposed replacements are unverified; the finding is phrased as a concrete proposal, not a claim about compilation.

    rw [dualEvalLie_base]

findings.problem: There is no simp lemma that turns a first-jet coordinate projection into its `dualEvalLie` value, and the two lemmas that do compute the base and tangent projections are not simp lemmas. The target therefore has to use the definitional `change` at lines 38/41 to replace `(polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord` by `dualEvalLie t h A.coord`, and then `rw [dualEvalLie_base]`/`rw [dualEvalLie_tangent]`; the same four-line block is duplicated for `A` and `C` and for the `U` and `V` goals at lines 84–101. Desired normal forms are: `dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord = eval t P.coord` and `dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord = eval t (directionalDerivative h P.coord)`. The relevant existing rules are `@[simp] polynomialFirstJet_base` (which already normalises the analogous `dualBaseHom` projection); `dualEvalLie_base` and `dualEvalLie_tangent`, which state exactly the needed underlying equalities but carry no attribute; and `NilpotentLieBCHGroup.map_coord`, a `rfl` projection lemma (`(map f g).coord = f g.coord`) that is neither annotated nor syntactically applicable here, since `polynomialFirstJetHom` is a plain `noncomputable def` that `simp` will not unfold to expose `map`.
findings.proposed_change: In RealPolynomialChartSubstitution.lean, next to `@[simp] polynomialFirstJet_base`, add the `rfl` projection lemma `@[simp] theorem polynomialFirstJet_coord_eq (t h : σ → ℚ) (P : PolynomialGroup σ hnil) : (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord = dualEvalLie t h P.coord := rfl`, and mark `dualEvalLie_base` and `dualEvalLie_tangent` `@[simp]` (their left-hand sides are distinct projection patterns reducing to `eval t p` and `eval t (directionalDerivative h p)`, with the existing `dualEvalLie_tmul`/`directionalDerivative_tmul` rules rewriting the arguments, so they fit the existing normal-form direction). The two bullets at lines 38–44 (and the four blocks at lines 84–101) would then become single `simpa only [polynomialFirstJet_coord_eq, dualEvalLie_base, eval_mem_iff_coefficients] using hAU`-style lines, with the tangent version using `dualEvalLie_tangent` and `directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule`. This should be compile-checked before adopting.
findings.benefit: Users would no longer need to reproduce the definitional equality behind `polynomialFirstJetHom`'s `.coord` field with `change` in order to reason about a first jet; `simp`/`simpa` would carry the two layer-membership goals (`U` for the base, `V` for the tangent) to `eval t P.coord ∈ _` and `eval t (directionalDerivative h P.coord) ∈ _` uniformly, removing the four duplicated `change`/`rw` blocks in this file and making the jet projection interface consistent with the already-`@[simp]` `polynomialFirstJet_base`.

evidence.excerpt:
noncomputable def polynomialFirstJetHom (t h : σ → ℚ) : PolynomialGroup σ hnil →* DualGroup hnil :=
  NilpotentLieBCHGroup.map (dualEvalLie t h)

@[simp] theorem polynomialFirstJet_base (t h : σ → ℚ) (P : PolynomialGroup σ hnil) :
    dualBaseHom (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P) = polynomialValueHom t P := by

theorem dualEvalLie_base (t h : σ → ℚ) (p : VectorPolynomial σ ℚ L) :
    dualBaseLinear (dualEvalLie t h p) = eval t p := by

theorem dualEvalLie_tangent [Fintype σ] (t h : σ → ℚ) (p : VectorPolynomial σ ℚ L) :
    dualTangentLinear (dualEvalLie t h p) = eval t (directionalDerivative h p) := by

theorem map_coord (f : L →ₗ⁅ℚ⁆ M) (g : NilpotentLieBCHGroup L s hL) :
    (map (hM := hM) f g).coord = f g.coord := rfl

have hz : dualTangentLinear (F.adaptedPolynomialJet h p).coord ∈
      F.shiftedPolynomialIdeal (fun _ : σ => 1) 1 := by
    rw [F.adaptedPolynomialJet_tangent]
